transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

Not necessarily. The first suspects are the battery not actually charging, the charger/contacts, or the vacuum protecting itself because airflow is restricted. Only after those are ruled out would an internal motor or electronics fault move up the list. The wording “red light flashing” is not a confirmed Dyson error code, so I cannot reliably assign it a specific meaning for your SV12 from that alone; it may simply be the battery’s warning indication. 1. Plug the charger directly into a known-good wall socket and make sure it is fully seated in the vacuum/dock. Wipe the charger and vacuum contacts with a clean, dry cloth. Look for any charging light while it is connected. No charging indication points more towards the charger, socket, contacts or battery. 2. With the vacuum switched off, remove the wand and floorhead, empty the bin, and check the bin inlet, wand and floorhead for a blockage. Clear hair from the brush bar and make sure it turns freely. A blockage can make a cordless Dyson shut down immediately. 3. Check the filters. If they are dirty, wash only as the filter instructions allow in cold water, then leave them to dry completely for at least 24 hours before refitting. Do not run it with a damp filter. If it still flashes red and will not run after it has most likely shown a normal charging indication and the airway is clear, the battery becomes the leading suspect—but I would not buy one until we know whether it shows a charge light when connected.

Tried those. The charger light is on in the hallway socket as well as the usual one, and the blue lights come on while it charges, but it still flashes red when I pull the trigger. No blockages, the bin's empty and I washed the filter last month. The battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly either. It's the original battery, about 4.5 years old, and the runtime had been dropping to about 8 minutes before it stopped.

Yes — a worn battery is a leading possibility on a cordless vacuum that will not run and flashes red at the trigger, particularly as the machine is older. It is not proof on its own, though: a charger, charging connection or internal fault can produce a very similar result. The red flashing light is not a confirmed Dyson error code here, so I cannot reliably assign it a specific SV12 meaning. It may be a battery warning rather than a fault code. Before deciding on a battery, check the charging indication: with the vacuum switched off, connect the charger directly and make sure it is fully seated. Wipe the contacts with a clean, dry cloth. If it shows no normal charging indication, suspect the charger, socket or contacts before the battery. If it appears to charge normally but still immediately flashes red and will not start, the battery becomes the most likely cause; an internal motor/control fault remains possible but is less common. Do not use or charge it if the battery becomes hot, swollen, leaks or smells unusual; that would need professional attention.
